{{Short description|German mathematician and astronomer}}
'''Carl Theodor Anger''' ([[Danzig]], 31 July 1803 – Danzig, 25 March 1858) was a German [[mathematician]] and [[astronomer]].<ref>Lawrynowicz (1995), p. 297.</ref> He was a student of and assistant to [[Friedrich Bessel]] at the [[Königsberg Observatory]] from 1827 until 1831.<ref>Lawrynowicz (1995), pp. 67–68.</ref> Thereafter, he was appointed as astronomer by the [[Danzig Research Society|Naturforschende Gesellschaft in Danzig]].<ref>Brandstäter (1858).</ref>

Besides his scientific work, especially that related to [[Bessel function]]s, he is also known for his first-hand biographical notes on the life of Bessel.
